title: OTLP ingest mediator that preserves sampling decisions and emits Tempo-friendly envelopes
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: Several customers ingest spans via OTLP (gRPC/HTTP) and downstream storage expects Tempo-style envelopes. Current OTLP->Tempo wiring strips certain sampling and legacy tags, causing incorrect tail-sampling and difficulty correlating with logs/metrics. We need a mediator that accepts OTLP, preserves per-span sampling hints/traceflags, normalizes legacy tag names, and emits Tempo-friendly span envelopes (with tenant headers) without blocking throughput targets.

Goals:
- Preserve sampling decisions (traceflags and explicit sampling tags) when converting to Tempo envelopes so downstream tail-samplers and retention rules behave correctly.
- Emit Tempo-compatible JSON envelopes with tenant and ingestion metadata, avoiding schema-violating transformations.
- Add a schema-evolution warning header so we can detect older clients sending deprecated fields.
- Keep p99 ingest latency under 75ms and not regress throughput beyond 5% at 95th percentile traffic.

Proposed design:
1) OTLP Ingest Mediator (new lightweight process in trace-ingest fleet):
   - Receives OTLP spans (grpc + http) and performs a fast, deterministic mapping to Tempo envelope without deep enrichment.
   - Copies traceflags and any span-level sampling tags (e.g., "sampling.priority", "otel.traces.sampling.priority") into the envelope metadata.
   - Provides a configurable normalization table for legacy tag keys (e.g., "svc" -> "service.name") loaded from S3; mismatch triggers a schema-evolution-warning boolean in envelope headers.
   - Emits to Tempo write endpoint using existing backpressure-aware writer (reuses code from ENG-271001 writer).

2) Non-functional safety nets:
   - Minimal synchronous validation to avoid dropping spans: if a span is malformed, enqueue to dead-letter queue (S3) and continue.
   - Circuit breaker that switches to a pass-through fanout (mirror original OTLP proto) if Tempo endpoint reports 5xx above threshold.

Tradeoffs considered:
- Enrichment vs. passthrough: We avoid heavy enrichment in the mediator to keep latency low; richer enrichment remains in the downstream span-processor.
- Strict schema adherence vs. compatibility: We intentionally maintain deprecated fields in a dedicated namespace to avoid breaking older queries while signaling their presence via warnings.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit/integration tests that verify sampling flags are present in Tempo envelopes for three sampler types (always, never, parent-based).
- End-to-end load test demonstrating p99 <= 75ms at 200k spans/s with current fleet config and <5% throughput regression versus baseline.
- Schema warning metrics emitted to datadog (metric: tracing.mediator.schema_warnings) and dashboard updated.
- Graceful fallback exercised in chaos run (simulate Tempo 503s) and verified that spans are mirrored into dead-letter with no data loss beyond the window.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): Deploy mediator in us-west-2 cluster, route 1% of OTLP traffic from internal test tenants (2 days). Monitor p99 latency, schema_warnings, and error rate.
- Phase 2 (regional expansion): 10% routing over multiple regions + compatibility checks for legacy clients (3 days).
- Phase 3 (global): Full rollout with automatic fallback policies and runbooks (1 day).

Monitoring & dashboards required:
- New dashboard: "Tracing Mediator - Ingest Health" with: ingest rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate to Tempo, schema_warning rate, deadletter enqueue rate.
- Add alert: p99 > 100ms sustained for 5m -> paging; 5xx to Tempo > 1% 10m -> P1.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Which deprecated tag keys do we preserve vs. coerce? (PM wants to keep >95% compatibility; engineering prefers explicit list).
- Should we sign envelopes with tenant signature (HMAC) for downstream verification? Security input required.
